title: CompliProof — two reconciled exports + P0 evidence checklist
purpose: Run the reconciliation command against the client's two systems. The 7 P0 production gates are infrastructure evidence, NOT CSVs.

files.required_columns: id (key, non-empty, no duplicates) + business columns
files.what_it_proves: System A side of the reconciliation

files.required_columns: id (key, non-empty, no duplicates) + matching business columns
files.what_it_proves: System B side of the reconciliation

files.required_columns: generated by CompliProof, not filled by the client
files.what_it_proves: Expected reconciliation shape (matched / A-only / B-only / mismatched)
The 7 open P0 gates and exactly what closes each one

reconcile_command: PYTHONPATH=src python -m compliproof.cli reconcile system_a.csv system_b.csv id

findings: key present only in system A - unmatched row preserved
key present only in system A - unmatched row preserved
key present only in system B - unmatched row preserved

cannot_generate: P0-1 Packaging / deployment — NO — needs a hosted CI run and a clean-runner install matrix
P0-2 Evidence integrity — NO — needs an independent reviewer and a non-symmetric key lifecycle
P0-3 Audit ledger — NO — needs an external timestamp anchor receipt (e.g. freetsa)
P0-4 Reporting / reconciliation — PARTIAL — the two CSVs let you run the reconciliation; the served report and audit event must be produced by CompliProof itself
P0-5 Server reporting — NO — needs routes, auth and a security scan
P0-6 Authentication — NO — needs a real auth implementation and security review
P0-7 Dashboard / UI security — NO — needs a browser acceptance test and route inventory
honesty: Simulated, format-exact template data. The client must replace ONLY the data rows with their own real rows and keep the header, column order and value conventions unchanged. Passing a validator does not make simulated data real compliance evidence.
